Have any of you purchased a "smart watch"? If so, which one and how do you like it?

I got a pebble as a reward for a pledge for Reading Rainbow on kickstarter. It was pretty cool, not enough apps or functionality. Construction felt "cheap". I think I've discovered I just don't like wearing a watch anymore though.
I had to bring it back, it was smarter than me :(

I have a G Watch R and I really like it. Its great for subtly checking messages and notification without pulling out your phone. I mostly got it because I liked the ability to get turn by turn GPS when I am on my motorcycle or bicycle. It will vibrate and show turns on the watch face so I don't need to have my phone out. There's also a lot of cool features that aren't really necessary but cool none the less. I can check out my home secuity cams with the TinyCam app, control my Sonos or music apps, there's also a remote shutter and viewfinder for your phone's camera, and you can even play solitaire or space invaders on it. The touchscreen is remarkably precise for being so small. It even has Wi-Fi so it can work when I don t have my phone. You can even swap out the watch bands for any other 22mm band. This is a pretty standard size for most sport watches today. Overall I would say Android wear is the way to go. Far more apps and functionality than Apple or Pebble.

I got the Microsoft Band. It's half way from a fitbit to a smart watch. Lots of great features for fitness. They even recently added something for golfing, which was fun. It has a great notification system that you can enable or disable any updates you want to see on the watch. If you have a Windows Phone, you can even text from the watch which is impressively accurate.

I have a Pebble Steel and I love it. The main killer apps are Music controll and the Google tasks manager.

Having direct music controll from my wrist and a checklist of work I need to accomplish that day in a nice easy to read list is a game changer. The Steel version looks professional and is more durable with gorilla glass.

Quick responses with email and text messages is also great. I can respond to both with personally programed responses in three clicks.
Same here. I really like my pebble steel. I use it for notifications, time and music...occasionally games like drag race to pass the time
I don't really see the point of smart watch. I wear a normal watch and have my phone for everything else.

I have the Gear Neo 2 and i love it. It fits my wrist really nice and i use the sleep tracking/stwp counting feature daily. Its also nice to feel a vibration on my arm if i get a text and my phone is in the other room. Useful at work to sneak texts :D

I owned the original Pebble and loved it. I don't need anything more than alerts, music control, and a timer. It does/did all that. I now have a pebble time and love it! Sure, it's really not much more than what the original pebble did, but somehow the color screen makes it all better and frankly it really does look amazing imo. I've considered switching to a watch with an LED screen, but there are 3 things that stop me. First and foremost is the screen itself. I want a watch I don't need to turn on to see. I can just glance and see it. Second is the battery life. The pebble series generally has a pretty good battery life. Depending on it's use, I typically get anywhere from 4-6 days out of the battery. Last is water resistance or rather it's water proof rating. I tend to wear my watch everywhere: showers, swimming, etc. I don't want to have to think about my watch when it's raining. Anyways, hoped all this info helped :-).

I have an apple watch, it will disappoint you if you are looking for a replacement for your phone. However, it makes a good companion to it. I don't have have to get me phone out as often, and I like being able to just glance at my watch to see if it is something that needs addressing right away. This is especially nice because I work from home.

I got an LG G watch when it was on sale for cheap. It's been useful skiing or at concerts when it's hard to keep my phone nearby like in a backpack. Knowing if it's worth my time to get my phone to respond to something has been nice. They are useful if thru are cheap but I don't think they are worth 300 currently.

Half truths as male-dominated jobs. Half truths as the 77 cent income average for women. Half truths about exploitation, sexual violence, and so on.

There are those that claim there's patriarchal sexism but honestly I feel that they're doing more harm than good - trying to find sexism in everything.
